14.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

15.meaning: So/then ask, inquire, request — to put a question or make a request. With the prefixed 'so/then', it issues this as a command following from what precedes.
15.grammar: A connecting/result particle fa- ('so, then') prefixed to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male ('you, ask!'). The bare, vowel-less ending is typical of the singular command form, telling one person to do the action.
15.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, inquire, request, seek

16.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

17.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
17.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
17.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

3.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

4.meaning: 'Prostrate! / bow down!' — a command to a group to lower themselves to the ground in prostration, the posture of deepest humility and submission.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb meaning 'prostrate / bow down'. It begins with a helping vowel (the initial 'u-') to ease pronunciation; the ending '-ū' (written with a silent trailing alif) directs the command to a plural 'you all'.
4.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down

5.meaning: 'To / for the All-Merciful.' Al-Rahman is a divine name of Allah denoting the One whose mercy is vast, all-embracing, and overflowing to the whole of creation; the prefixed 'to/for' directs an action or dedication toward Him.
5.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('to / for'). Because li- demands the genitive case, the noun takes the final -i ending. The article al- assimilates into the following 'r' sound (heard as ar-Rahman). The form al-Rahman is an intensive pattern signifying overwhelming, all-encompassing mercy.

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: The Most Gracious / All-Merciful (al-Raḥmān) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in an intensive pattern denoting mercy that is vast, all-encompassing, and overflowing to all creation.
8.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

9.meaning: A question: 'shall we prostrate?' — the act of sajdah, bowing down with the forehead to the ground in worship and total submission, asked by a group about themselves ('we').
9.grammar: Present-tense verb with 'we' as subject: the a- at the front turns the statement into a question, and the na- prefix means 'we'. The final -u is the normal present-tense (indicative) ending, marking a plain ongoing or intended action rather than a command or wish.

10.meaning: 'Regarding what / as to that which'. A compound joining the preposition 'to/for/regarding' with the relative pronoun 'what / that which', introducing a clause about a thing or matter.
10.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'to', 'for', or 'regarding'. 'mā' is a relative pronoun meaning 'what' or 'that which', used for things and ideas (not persons). It has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'You command us' — the act of ordering or bidding, directed by one person ('you') at a group ('us'). The root gives words like amr (a command, an affair).
11.grammar: Present-tense verb: ta- means 'you', the stem is 'command', and -nā tacked on the end means 'us' — Arabic attaches object pronouns directly to the verb. The -u- vowel before -nā is the regular present-tense (indicative) ending.

12.meaning: 'And it increased them' — the idea of adding to, augmenting, making something grow greater in someone; a completed action whose object is 'them'.
12.grammar: Past-tense verb, third person ('he/it increased'): in Arabic the bare past form with no prefix already means 'he/it did'. The -hum on the end is the object pronoun 'them' attached directly to the verb, so one word carries 'and + increased + them'.

13.meaning: Aversion, flight, or shrinking away — a turning-away in revulsion or estrangement; recoiling from something.
13.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). Here the accusative often serves as a 'specification' answering 'in what respect?' — e.g. increasing someone 'in aversion'. The noun names the action/state of fleeing or shrinking away.
13.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to flee, shy away, recoil, be averse

1.meaning: He is blessed; He is exalted, abundant in good, and the source of all blessing and increase. This special verb form is reserved for praising Allah, conveying that He is supremely abundant in goodness and far above all else in majesty.

parts.en: He is blessed / exalted in abundance

1.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ("He …"), of the form tafāʿala, here expressing an intensive state of being abundantly blessed and exalted. The -a ending marks the standard third-person masculine singular past.
1.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — blessing, abundance, growth, lasting good

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
5.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'towers' or 'lofty structures,' and in the language of the sky, the great constellations or stations of the heavens — imposing, elevated formations.
6.grammar: 'Burūj' is a broken (irregular) plural of burj ('tower'). The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) typically marks an indefinite noun functioning as the object of a verb ('… towers/constellations').
6.root: ب-ر-ج (b-r-j) — to be prominent, lofty, to tower up

7.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
7.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

8.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

9.meaning: A lamp — a burning, radiant source of light; in Qur'anic usage sirāj often evokes the blazing sun itself, a lamp hung in the sky.
9.grammar: Indefinite noun with the -an ending: the doubled final vowel (tanwīn) means 'a lamp' (not 'the lamp'), and the a-vowel is the accusative case, the form a noun typically takes as the object of a verb ('made/placed a lamp').
9.root: س-ر-ج (s-r-j) — lamp, to give blazing light

10.meaning: 'And a moon' — qamar is the moon, whose root also colors words for whiteness and moonlit brightness.
10.grammar: The wa- prefix is the ordinary 'and'. The -an ending is indefinite ('a moon') and accusative — the case a noun typically carries when it is the object of a verb, matching a preceding object it is joined to by 'and'.

11.meaning: Light-giving, luminous, shining — not merely bright in itself but actively casting light on other things; a describing word from the same root as nūr (light).

parts.en: light-giving, illuminating (the doubled m only echoes the ending of the preceding word in recitation)

11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'one that gives light') from the causative verb anāra, 'to give light'. The mu- beginning is the participle marker for that verb type; the shadda (doubling) written on the initial m is not part of the word itself but a recitation link (idghām), where the -n of a preceding tanwīn merges into this m. The -an ending is indefinite accusative, agreeing with the noun it describes — adjectives copy the case of their noun.

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

4.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
4.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

5.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.

6.meaning: Succession, alternation — the state of two things following one another in turns, each taking the other's place (as night and day replace each other). From the root of khalīfah, 'one who comes after / a successor'.
6.grammar: A noun of state or manner. The -atan ending combines the feminine marker -a(t) with indefinite accusative tanwīn; the accusative here typically works adverbially — describing the manner or condition in which something is made or exists ('in alternation').
6.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, replace

7.meaning: A combined expression meaning 'to whom?' or 'for whom?' — it asks about the owner or the one to whom something belongs. It fuses the preposition 'to/for' with the question word 'who'.
7.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the interrogative 'who'. Together they pose the question 'to whom (does it belong)?'. The combination is fixed in form and does not change its ending.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
8.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
8.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: 'That he take heed / be reminded' — an intensive, reflexive remembering: to let a reminder actually sink in, reflect, and take the lesson to heart, not merely recall a fact.
10.grammar: A Form V verb (originally yatadhakkara; the ta- has assimilated into the dh, doubling it — hence the heavy -dhdh-). This verb form adds a sense of working something on oneself: making oneself remember. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, the shape a present verb takes after particles meaning 'that / in order to', signaling purpose or intention rather than a plain statement.

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
12.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
12.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

13.meaning: Thankfulness, gratitude — shukr in an intensive noun pattern suggesting abundant, heartfelt giving of thanks; recognizing a favor and responding to it.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (the action itself as a thing: 'thanking, gratitude'). The -an ending is indefinite accusative, the case typically borne by the object of a verb or of an intention ('desires/intends gratitude').
13.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to thank, be grateful

1.meaning: 'And the slaves/servants of…' — ʿibād is the plural of ʿabd, a slave or bondservant. Applied to people before Allah it is a title of honor: those who belong wholly to their Lord and devote themselves to His service.
1.grammar: The -u ending is the nominative case: the form a noun takes when it is the subject — the one being talked about — of a sentence. It carries no tanwīn (no -un) because the word is about to be linked to a following word in an 'X of Y' construction ('the servants of…').
1.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a slave

2.meaning: The Most Merciful, the All-Compassionate — a name of Allah on an intensive pattern stressing immense, all-embracing mercy that encompasses the whole of creation. It denotes overflowing, universal compassion rather than an occasional act of kindness.
2.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'; its 'l' assimilates in pronunciation into the following 'r' (heard as ar-raḥmān). The word is an intensive form on the faʿlān pattern, conveying fullness and vastness of the quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, used when a word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… OF …').

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They walk / they go on foot' — a present-tense verb for walking, moving along, or going by foot.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' walking now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.
4.root: م-ش-ي (m-sh-y) — to walk, go on foot

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

7.meaning: Gentleness, unassuming ease, humility — hawn is a calm, dignified lightness of manner, free of arrogance and harshness; used adverbially it means 'gently, humbly'.
7.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (-an). This accusative typically works adverbially, describing the manner of an action — 'in gentleness', i.e. 'gently, humbly' — rather than naming a thing acted upon.

8.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

9.meaning: 'He addressed them / spoke to them' — the verb of direct address (Form III of the root of khuṭbah, a speech), meaning to speak to someone face to face, often confrontationally.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb, third person ('he addressed'); the long ā after the first letter marks Form III, the pattern of actions directed at another person. The attached -hum means 'them'; its extra final -u is just a helping vowel Arabic adds to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a joining alif.
9.root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b) — to address, deliver a speech

10.meaning: 'The ignorant ones' — jāhil describes not just lack of knowledge but jāhiliyyah-style behavior: rash, uncouth, foolish conduct that ignores truth and courtesy.
10.grammar: An active participle ('one who acts ignorantly') made plural. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case: it marks 'more than two men/people' serving as the subject — the doers — of a verb. (Were the word an object or after a preposition, it would end -īna instead.)

11.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

12.meaning: Peace / a greeting of peace / safety and security. It names peace and well-being, and serves as the word of greeting and goodwill ('peace (be upon you)').
12.grammar: A noun with the final -an ending, which marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or, as often here, for a word said by way of greeting or stating a manner ('(saying) peace').

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They pass the night' — the verb bāta means to spend the night, to be occupied in some state through the night hours; from the same root as bayt, 'house' (where one passes the night).

parts.en: third person prefix (marks 'he/they'; the plural sense comes from the ending)

2.grammar: Present-tense verb: the ya- prefix marks third person, and it is the -ūna ending that supplies the plural 'they' — together they mean 'they (a group of people) do it now / habitually'. The full -ūna ending is the plain indicative form — a straightforward statement of what they regularly do; it would be clipped to -ū after words like 'that' or 'not'.
2.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to pass the night; house

3.meaning: For / to their Lord — directed toward the Lord (Rabb): the One who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures, guiding His creation to its completion. The phrase links an attitude or action to Him.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') puts the noun in the genitive case (seen in the -i of rabbi). 'Rabb' is then joined to the possessive suffix -him ('their,' masculine plural). The whole phrase marks a relation directed toward the Lord.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining mastery

4.meaning: 'Prostrating' / 'in prostration' — bowing down low with the face to the ground, the posture of deepest humility and worship. A plural describing a group in that humble, bowed state.
4.grammar: A plural active descriptor ('those prostrating'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which here works adverbially — describing the manner or state in which the subject acts (i.e. doing something 'while prostrating'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive plural pattern used for a group performing the action.
4.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

5.meaning: 'And standing' — qiyām means standing upright; as a plural of qāʾim, 'those standing', it evokes people on their feet, classically in long night prayer.
5.grammar: Joined by wa- ('and') to a preceding word of the same shape. The -an ending is indefinite accusative; this accusative typically describes the state or posture in which the subject performs an action ('while standing'), a common adverb-like use of the case.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

3.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

3.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

4.meaning: 'Avert! Turn away!' — a plea-command from ṣarafa, to turn something aside, deflect it, make it pass away from someone.

parts.en: helping vowel that starts the command form

4.grammar: An imperative (command form) addressed to one person: 'you — avert!'. The initial i- is only a pronunciation aid, not part of the root. The bare, vowel-less ending (the final f closes with sukūn, no case vowel) is exactly what marks the singular command in Arabic; in usage such a command form can serve equally as an order or as an earnest plea.
4.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert

5.meaning: "from us / on our behalf" — ʿan is the preposition 'from / away from / concerning,' and the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'from us' (often in the sense of pardoning faults away from us).
5.grammar: A preposition ('from / away from') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The n of ʿan blends into the n of -nā (written doubled). It conveys moving away from, or being concerning, the thing named.

6.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

7.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
7.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
7.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

8.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
8.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

9.meaning: 'Its punishment / its torment' — ʿadhāb is painful chastisement, and the attached 'its/her' points back to some feminine thing whose punishment it is.
9.grammar: Noun plus possessor: the -hā suffix means 'its' (referring to something grammatically feminine), turning 'punishment' into 'its punishment'. The -a vowel before -hā is the accusative case ending, the form a noun typically takes as the object of a verb ('avert its punishment'). Because a possessor is attached, there is no tanwīn.

10.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

10.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

11.meaning: Clinging, inseparable — gharām is something that fastens onto a person and will not let go, like an unpayable debt (same root as gharīm, 'debtor'); hence an ever-adhering, permanent anguish.
11.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (-an); in this use the accusative typically predicates a quality of something already mentioned — declaring what something is or is like ('it is ever-clinging') — a standard function of the case after verbs of being.
11.root: غ-ر-م (gh-r-m) — to cling like a debt; loss, liability

1.meaning: 'Indeed it (is)…' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with an attached feminine pronoun 'it/she'. inna firmly asserts and stresses the statement that follows.
1.grammar: An emphasis particle (inna) plus an attached pronoun, third person feminine singular (-hā). inna introduces and strengthens a nominal statement, and the suffixed -hā is its 'ism' (the noun governed by inna), which inna places in the accusative case. So although -hā corresponds to the English subject ('indeed it/she …'), grammatically it is the accusative ism of inna, not a nominative subject.

2.meaning: 'Evil is it! / How wretched it is' — the verb sāʾa states that something is bad, vile, grievous; Arabic often uses it as an exclamation of condemnation: 'what an evil … it is!'.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb with the -t suffix marking a feminine subject: 'she/it (something feminine) is evil'. Arabic uses this past form timelessly for verdicts of praise or blame — like English 'How evil is…!' — so the past tense here signals a settled judgment, not a bygone event.

3.meaning: A settled abode — mustaqarr is a place (or state) of settling down and remaining fixed; from the root of qarār, 'settledness, rest'.
3.grammar: A noun of place from the Form X verb istaqarra, 'to settle down and stay'; the musta- beginning is that verb-form's participle/place marker. The -an ending is indefinite accusative, the case used for the noun that completes an exclamation of blame or serves as a verb's object ('evil as an abode').
3.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, remain, be fixed

4.meaning: 'And a place of staying' — muqām is a residence, a station where one stays; from aqāma, 'to stay, take up residence' (same root as qiyām, standing).
4.grammar: wa- is 'and', joining this noun to a preceding one of the same shape. The mu- beginning marks a noun of place from the verb aqāma ('to reside'). The -an ending is indefinite accusative, matching the noun it is paired with — nouns joined by 'and' share the same case.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, stay, reside

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'when / whenever' — a particle pointing to a time, usually a future or expected occasion ('at the time that ...').
2.grammar: A time particle ('when, whenever') that introduces a clause and points to the moment something happens, typically expected or recurring. It sets up a 'when X, then Y' relationship and does not itself alter word endings.

3.meaning: 'They spent / disbursed' — the act of laying out wealth, giving it away, or expending it, done by a group in the past.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in a pattern meaning to spend or expend (especially wealth). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, disburse

4.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

4.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
4.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: 'They are (not) extravagant' — asrafa means to go to excess, to overshoot the proper limit, especially in spending; isrāf is wasteful excess.

parts.en: third person prefix (marks 'he/they'; its u-vowel signals a Form IV verb — the plural sense comes from the ending)

5.grammar: Present-tense verb: the yu- prefix marks third person (its u-vowel marking the Form IV verb asrafa), while the plural 'they' is carried by the -ū suffix. Note the ending: -ū alone, not the full -ūna. The dropped -na is the clipped (subjunctive/jussive) form that a plural present verb takes after particles like lam ('did not'), lā of prohibition, or an ('that') — so the very shape of the word shows it follows such a particle.

6.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
6.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

7.meaning: 'They are (not) stingy' — qatara means to be tight-fisted and miserly, to withhold and spend too little, the opposite extreme from extravagance.

parts.en: third person prefix (marks 'he/they'; the plural sense comes from the ending)

7.grammar: Present-tense verb: ya- marks third person, and the plural 'they' is carried by the clipped -ū ending (the full form would be -ūna): a plural present verb loses its final -na after particles such as lam, lā, or an, so this shape signals the verb stands under such a particle's influence — typically a negation.

8.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

9.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
10.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

11.meaning: A just middle course, balanced moderation — qawām is the upright, evenly-poised point between two extremes; from the root of 'standing straight'.
11.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (-an). This accusative typically predicates or describes the state of something already mentioned — 'being (in) a balanced middle way' — a regular use of the case for stating what something is or how it stands.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand upright, be balanced

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
3.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

4.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
4.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
6.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
6.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

7.meaning: Another, other, a different one — a further item distinct from the one already mentioned.
7.grammar: An adjective/noun meaning 'other'. It belongs to a small group of words that resist the usual indefinite -n (nunation), so even when indefinite it takes a plain -a ending. That final -a is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or one in agreement with such a noun.
7.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after, other

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: 'They kill / they slay' — a present/future verb describing a group taking life or putting others to death.
9.grammar: A Form I present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks the plural 'they' subject. The full -ūna (with final nūn) is the indicative, the plain ongoing present/future form used when no particle shortens it.
9.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

10.meaning: 'The soul / self / life' — the living person or inner self; by extension a human life.
10.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), which is why the 'n' is doubled in pronunciation (an-nafs). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. It denotes the self, the soul, or a living person.

11.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
11.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

12.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
13.root: — (proper divine name)

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
15.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
15.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: They commit zinā — unlawful sexual intercourse, any sexual relations outside the bond of marriage. The verb describes the act itself as an ongoing or habitual practice.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'they (masculine plural)'. The ya- prefix marks third person in the present/ongoing tense, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood — a plain statement of what they do or keep doing.

18.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
18.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

19.meaning: He does, makes, or carries out; the doing or performing of an act. A general verb for engaging in or committing some deed.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks the singular male subject. The final consonant carries no vowel (the jussive/conditional form), which is the shortened form a present verb takes after conditional or certain other particles, typically giving the sense 'if/whoever does…'.
19.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

20.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
20.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

21.meaning: He will meet, encounter, come face to face with — running into something so that it confronts you directly.
21.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'he'. The ya- prefix means 'he'. The clipped ending — short -a where the full form would be yalqā with a long vowel — marks the jussive mood, the shortened form a verb takes as the outcome of a condition ('whoever does X ... will meet Y') or after certain particles.

22.meaning: A penalty for sin — the painful requital that sin itself earns; some scholars said it names a specific punishment, others simply the due recompense of wrongdoing.
22.grammar: Indefinite noun with the -an accusative ending: the accusative typically marks the direct object — the thing the verb lands on (what is met, received, given) — and the -n sound (nunation) makes it indefinite, 'a penalty' rather than 'the penalty'.

1.meaning: It will be doubled, multiplied over and over — made to grow in repeated increments rather than simply added once.
1.grammar: Passive present-tense verb, 'it'. The yu- prefix with the internal a-vowels marks the passive voice: the subject has the doubling done TO it. The vowel-less (sukūn) ending marks the jussive mood, the form a verb takes in the result of a condition ('whoever ... , it will be doubled').

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
3.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.
3.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

4.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
4.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

5.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
5.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: And he will remain forever — abide permanently, dwell without end. Khulūd is unending permanence in a state or place.
6.grammar: wa- is 'and', joining this verb to what precedes. ya- means 'he'. The vowel-less (sukūn) ending marks the jussive mood — the shortened verb form used for the outcome of a condition, continuing the same chain as the verbs before it.

7.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

8.meaning: Humiliated, disgraced, held in contempt — one who has been stripped of honour and made low.
8.grammar: A passive participle: the mu- prefix builds 'one to whom the action is done' — here, one who is treated with contempt. The -an accusative ending with nunation typically marks a state or condition ('in a humiliated state') or a direct object, and makes the word indefinite.

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: "he turned back (in repentance) / repented" — a completed-action verb of turning away from wrongdoing and returning (to Allah); when said of Allah toward a person, it means He turned to them in mercy and accepted their repentance.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"). The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer. The hollow root's middle weak letter appears as a long "ā" in this form.
3.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

4.meaning: And he believed; to have faith, to trust and affirm as true, to commit oneself in belief. Carries the sense of inner conviction together with security and trust given to what one accepts.
4.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. This is a past-tense (completed) verb in Form IV (the lengthened ā- pattern), meaning 'he came to have faith / believed'. With no attached subject ending, it defaults to 'he' (third-person masculine singular). Form IV here links the believer to the object of faith with trust.
4.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

5.meaning: "And he did / worked / acted" — to do or perform an action, to put work into effect. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he did'. The bare -a ending with no attached pronoun marks this completed, masculine 'he' action. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

6.meaning: A deed / an action — a thing done, a work or act performed. The word names the action itself, stated indefinitely ('a deed').
6.grammar: A noun, 'deed/work/action'. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a deed') and accusative in case — the form typically used for the object of a verb or to specify 'as/in respect of'.
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; a deed

7.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
7.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

8.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

9.meaning: He changes, replaces, exchanges one thing for another — the intensive verb form suggests a thorough substitution, swapping something out entirely.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'he'. The yu- prefix means 'he'; the doubled middle letter (baddil) is the intensive verb pattern, giving the sense of deliberately and thoroughly exchanging. The final -u marks the indicative mood — a straightforward statement of fact, not a command or condition.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: Their evil deeds, misdeeds, or wrongs — bad actions and the harm or offence they carry; with the attached pronoun, the misdeeds belonging to them.
11.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun (singular sayyiʾa) with the attached possessive 'their'. The -i vowel before -him reflects the genitive/possessive linkage to that pronoun.

12.meaning: Good deeds, good things — plural of ḥasana, a single act of goodness or beauty that counts in one's favour.
12.grammar: A feminine plural noun: the -āt suffix is the regular feminine plural ('good deeds'). Its final -in is the ending such -āt plurals take for both the genitive case (after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship) and the accusative (direct object), with nunation marking it as indefinite.

13.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

16.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: "he turned back (in repentance) / repented" — a completed-action verb of turning away from wrongdoing and returning (to Allah); when said of Allah toward a person, it means He turned to them in mercy and accepted their repentance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"). The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer. The hollow root's middle weak letter appears as a long "ā" in this form.
2.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

3.meaning: "And he did / worked / acted" — to do or perform an action, to put work into effect. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he did'. The bare -a ending with no attached pronoun marks this completed, masculine 'he' action. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.
3.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work / do / act

4.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
4.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

5.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

6.meaning: 'He/it turns in relenting / accepts repentance' — from tāba; of Allah it means He relents toward and accepts the return of a servant; of a person, he turns back to Allah.
6.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix marks a masculine singular subject, 'he/it.' The final -u ending is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) marker, indicating an action that is happening or customary.
6.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

7.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
7.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: A true returning — repentance as an act of turning back to Allah. It is the verbal noun of tāba 'to turn in repentance', naming the return itself.
9.grammar: A verbal noun on the ma- pattern, naming the action of turning back. The -an accusative ending with nunation typically emphasises or completes the meaning of a related verb ('turns ... with a true turning') and marks the word as indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'they bear witness / testify' — a group giving firm testimony or attesting to the truth of something.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural). The -ūna ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense for a plural subject ('they bear witness / do testify').
3.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

4.meaning: Falsehood — al-zūr covers lying testimony, vain and false speech, and by extension gatherings of falsehood; speech or scenes that deviate from the truth.
4.grammar: Definite noun: al- means 'the', and because zūr begins with a 'sun letter' the l sound merges into the z (az-zūr). The final -a marks the accusative case, the case of the direct object — the thing witnessed, attended, or acted upon.
4.root: ز-و-ر (z-w-r) — deviation, falsehood (also visiting)

5.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
5.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

6.meaning: They passed, went by — moving past something rather than stopping at it or joining in.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb: the -ū suffix means 'they (masculine plural)' and marks the completed past — 'they passed'. The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention only, not pronounced.

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for/by what is idle and unintended (in speech)' — careless, thoughtless utterance that carries no firm intent, such as an oath blurted out without resolve. The prefix marks it as the basis or cause of an action.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('for, by, on account of') joined to a definite noun ('the …'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition. 'Laghw' denotes vain, purposeless, or unintended talk.
7.root: ل-غ-و (l-gh-w) — idle/vain talk, nonsense, the unintended

8.meaning: They passed, went by — moving past something rather than stopping at it or joining in.
8.grammar: Past-tense verb: the -ū suffix means 'they (masculine plural)' and marks the completed past — 'they passed'. The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention only, not pronounced.

9.meaning: Noble, dignified, honourable ones — plural of karīm, one marked by nobility of character and generosity, too dignified to be soiled by what is low.
9.grammar: A plural adjective used as a noun. The -an accusative ending with nunation typically marks a state or manner — describing HOW an action is done ('... as dignified ones') — and shows the word is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: A passive past-tense verb meaning 'they were reminded / admonished.' The intensive form of the root means to have something brought back to one's mind and conscience — to be called to remember and take heed.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the passive voice — the vowel pattern (u–i) shows the subject had the action done to them ('they were reminded') rather than doing it. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'they.' The doubled middle root letter gives the intensive sense of being earnestly admonished.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention; to remind, admonish

4.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
4.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
4.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

5.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
5.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

6.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

6.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

7.meaning: They fall down, collapse, drop to the ground — kharra pictures falling with force or suddenness, often of falling prostrate.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'they'. The ya- prefix marks third person present; the -ū marks a masculine plural subject. The absence of the usual final -na (yakhirrūna would be the plain indicative) signals a non-indicative mood — the shortened form verbs take after negating or subordinating particles. The silent alif after -ū is spelling only.

8.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
8.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

9.meaning: Deaf ones — plural of aṣamm, one whose hearing is blocked; used of those who will not truly listen.
9.grammar: A plural adjective. The -an accusative ending with nunation typically marks a state or manner — describing the condition someone is in while acting ('... as deaf ones') — and marks the word as indefinite.

10.meaning: And blind ones — plural of aʿmā, one who cannot see; used of those whose inner sight is shut to the truth.
10.grammar: wa- is 'and', pairing this word with the one before it. The -an accusative ending with nunation marks the same state/manner function as its partner word ('... and as blind ones') and shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

3.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

3.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

4.meaning: A command meaning 'grant!' or 'bestow!' — a request to give or confer something as a gift, typically addressed to Allah in supplication.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a single person: 'grant!'. The verb's weak first root letter drops in the command form, leaving the short, vowel-less ending — the standard shape of a direct request to one addressee.
4.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — giving freely, bestowing a gift

5.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
5.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: Our spouses / our mates (of) — husbands or wives, pairs, partners; the plural 'spouses' bound to the possessor 'our.'
7.grammar: A plural noun with the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as either following a preposition or linked to/possessed by what follows; here the attached pronoun -nā ('our') is the possessor. The genitive is also the case used after particles like li- ('for') and ʿalā ('upon').
7.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, mate, spouse, to join in a pair

8.meaning: And our offspring, our descendants — dhurriyya covers children and the generations that spring from a person.
8.grammar: wa- is 'and'. dhurriyyāt is a feminine plural (-āt suffix). The -i case vowel is the form -āt plurals take in the genitive and accusative — after a preposition, in an 'of' phrase, or as a direct object. The attached pronoun -nā means 'our', so the whole is 'and our descendants'.
8.root: ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-ʾ) — creating, scattering forth; hence progeny

9.meaning: Coolness, refreshment — qurrat ʿayn, 'coolness of the eye', is the Arabic idiom for deep comfort and delight: the eye settles, cool and at rest, on what it loves.
9.grammar: A noun in the construct state — the form a noun takes when linked to a following word as 'comfort OF ...' — which is why it carries no nunation. The final -a marks the accusative case, the case of the direct object (the thing asked for, given, or made).
9.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — coolness, settling, being at rest

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'eyes' — the plural of the word for eye, which can also mean a spring of water or the essence/self of a thing.
10.grammar: A plural noun. Its ending '-in' (written with tanwīn) combines the genitive case (linking it to a preceding word, as in 'delight OF eyes') with indefiniteness — 'eyes' in general rather than 'the eyes.'

11.meaning: "and make us / and appoint us" — a plea: 'render us into,' 'cause us to become,' or 'set us as.' The verb 'jaʿala' means to make, form, render, or appoint something into a state or role.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you,' with an attached object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The 'wa-' is the connector 'and.' The vowelless ending on the verb stem (sukūn) is characteristic of the imperative. 'jaʿala' often takes two objects: the thing made and what it is made into.
11.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

12.meaning: For the people of taqwā — the God-conscious, those who are mindful and careful of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing out of awareness of Him. The whole word means 'for/to the God-conscious ones'.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

12.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, prefixed by the preposition 'li-' ('for/to') and the definite article 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural form, used after a preposition; it means 'the (several) ones who…'. The base verb form (Form VIII) carries a reflexive sense: those who shield or protect themselves.
